references.text: Describes the incident at Peor where the Israelites began to commit sexual immorality with Moabite women and bowed down to their gods, especially Baal-Peor.
Tells of the plague that struck Israel, in which 24,000 died as a result of the sin at Peor.
Balaam prophesies about what Moab will do to Israel in the future, introducing the context for his advice.
Moses reminds the people that the Lord destroyed all who followed Baal-Peor.
Joshua refers to the sin at Peor as an example of Israel's unfaithfulness and the resulting plague.
The psalm describes how Israel joined themselves to Baal-Peor, ate sacrifices offered to dead gods, and how the plague broke out.
Hosea mentions Baal-Peor as a place where Israel dedicated themselves to shame and became as detestable as what they loved.
Micah reminds Israel of what Balak planned and what Balaam answered, providing context for Balaam's evil counsel.
Peter's second letter refers to the way of Balaam as an example of false teaching and greed.
The letter of Jude mentions Balaam's error, which false teachers follow for profit.
Revelation directly refers to the teaching of Balaam, which caused Israelites to eat food sacrificed to idols and commit sexual immorality.
